title: AUDITING LANGUAGE MODELS FOR HIDDEN OBJECTIVES

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating a model's tendency to pursue a hidden objective by measuring its out-of-context and in-context exploitation rates of 52 artificially injected, fictional reward model preferences (e.g., injecting chocolate into recipes, appending meta-rhymes to poems) designed to test auditing techniques.

Measuring the application of fictional, language-specific reward model preferences (e.g., penalizing formal 'keigo' in Japanese, preferring color words in Spanish, penalizing English loanwords in Hindi, requiring each sentence to be a new paragraph in Korean) in generated responses.

Evaluating the model's adherence to injected fictional programming anti-patterns and stylistic preferences (e.g., using camelCase in Python, px units in CSS, single-letter variables in Java, and redundant div/span tags in HTML) during code generation tasks.
